pr_title: Create "hashed" unit names from long paths
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/18077.

This will allow systemd to manage units (mounts, devices, swaps) that are created from external sources (e.g. /proc/swaps) and we couldn't represent them so far.

I haven't seen this before.  I dislike the fact that the hash overwrites the tail of the original path name. More often than not, the most distinctive portion of a device path is at the tail, while the front components of the path are just directories that are common to many devices. This will matter in particular for log messages, making it hard for users to figure out what device a given unit name actually maps to. Or am I overlooking something?

This is an edge case when everything is fucked anyway. Usability is long out of the window when this edge case is hit. If you actually care about user friendliness of any of this: don't generate crazy long paths like this in the kernel.

issue_context.title: RFE: support for long unit names
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
systemd currently has a hard limit of 255 bytes for the length of a unit name.  This causes problems such as #17684.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Longer unit names are supported.  This can be done by hashing them before converting them to a filename.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Long mount point paths could be handled differently.  For instance, they could be symlinked to somewhere under `/run`.
